subject: ylim() subsets data for display of boxplots

messages.author: daf017f67eba24e8
messages.subject: ylim() subsets data for display of boxplots
parts:
Hi-

There was a post with this same subject line, which suggested giving
an extended error message because ylim() subsets the data boxplotted
to within the specified range. This is a really great idea which can
save the ggplotter from making disastorously incorrect assumptions
about how the data looks - if the warning goes unheeded and
unexplored, since what is going on is not entirely clear.

However, there was no discussion of how to force the boxplot to be
computed on a different range than ylim() while only being plotted
within ylim(). In other words the IQR (and all outliers) will always
be within ylim(). How can one plot within ylim() of scale_y_continuous
(limit=) while representing the boxplot of the full data even if that
lies outside ylim? I've tried some things, nothing is working. Here's
a simple example:

## say you are calculating some stat via two different models/
methods
method1 <- rnorm(1000,mean=4,sd=1)
method2 <- rnorm(1000,mean=2,sd=10)
results=melt(data.frame(method1,method2))

## this is how the distributions really look
bp <-
ggplot( results, aes(variable,value)) +
geom_boxplot()
print(bp)

## this is a misrepresentation of the results of method2
## what is desired is focusing attention on the range ylim(0,10) which
would show the method 2 stats IQR
## dropping below this to some unseen lower limit... but instead we
see something else.
bp2 <-
ggplot( results, aes(variable,value)) +
geom_boxplot() +
scale_y_continuous(limit=c(0,10),drop=F)
print(bp2)


Thanks,

James

messages.subject: Re: ylim() subsets data for display of boxplots
parts:
On Thu, Jan 28, 2010 at 10:44 AM, McCreight <mccr...@gmail.com> wrote:
> However, there was no discussion of how to force the boxplot to be
> computed on a different range than ylim() while only being plotted
> within ylim().

You want the ylim= parameter to coord_cartesian(). Unfortunately, you
then have to set your own breaks and margins. Thus:

## this is how the distributions really look
bp <- ggplot( results, aes(variable,value)) + geom_boxplot()

## this is a misrepresentation of the results of method2
bp2 <- bp + scale_y_continuous(limit=c(0,10))

## this is the desired rendering
bp3 <- bp + scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0,10,by=2)) +
coord_cartesian(ylim=c(-0.5, 10.5))

## "multiple plots on the same page" recipe from the ggplot book
grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout=grid.layout(1, 3)))
vplayout = function(x, y) viewport(layout.pos.row=x, layout.pos.col=y)
print(bp, vp=vplayout(1,1))
print(bp2, vp=vplayout(1,2))
print(bp3, vp=vplayout(1,3))


zw
